planting.note: Plant grafted trees in early spring in deep, well-drained soil in full sun; Bernice sheds pollen early, so pair it with a later-blooming heartnut such as Ernie or Imshu for full pollination.

directions: Bernice, cataloged by Grimo Nut Nursery as selection Grimo 146, is a heartnut chosen for a wide internal cavity that lets the kernel drop free in whole, heart-shaped halves rather than fragmenting during cracking. It sheds pollen early in the season, before its own female flowers open, so growers pair it with a later-blooming heartnut cultivar such as Ernie or Imshu to ensure full nut set. Like other heartnuts, it should be planted in deep, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun, well away from juglone-sensitive garden plants.

planting.note: Plant grafted trees in early spring in deep, well-drained soil in full sun; Ernie is an early pollen shedder best used as a pollinizer for later-blooming heartnut cultivars.

directions: Ernie, Grimo Nut Nursery selection Grimo 89, produces a medium-sized nut with a reported 29 percent kernel fill that drops cleanly from the shell when cracked. It is an early pollen shedder, releasing pollen before its own female flowers become receptive, so it functions best as an early-season pollinizer for later-blooming heartnut cultivars rather than as a stand-alone tree. Grow it in deep, well-drained soil in full sun with a compatible heartnut nearby for reliable annual cropping.

planting.note: Plant grafted trees in early spring in deep, well-drained soil in full sun alongside a second heartnut cultivar for pollination.

directions: Killdeer is a Kentucky-origin heartnut selection offered by Grimo Nut Nursery, credited to grower Fred Blankenship and valued for medium-sized nuts that crack reliably into whole kernels. It is still being evaluated for performance in colder northern climates, so growers at the upper end of heartnut hardiness should treat it as a trial selection rather than a fully proven cultivar. Plant it in full sun in deep, fertile, well-drained soil alongside another heartnut cultivar for pollination.

planting.note: Plant grafted trees in early spring in deep, well-drained soil in full sun; pair with a later-flowering heartnut for pollination.

directions: Papple's Hope, registered by Grimo Nut Nursery as Grimo 99, is noted for the highest kernel yield among the nursery's heartnut selections, cracking out to roughly 34 percent kernel from a smooth internal cavity that releases the nutmeat with little effort. It sheds pollen before its own flowers are receptive, so it is best grown with a later-flowering heartnut for cross-pollination. Site it in full sun in deep, well-drained soil away from vegetable beds, since heartnut, like its black walnut relatives, produces juglone.

planting.note: Plant grafted trees, often on black walnut rootstock, in early spring in deep, well-drained soil in full sun with a second heartnut nearby for pollination.

directions: Patenaude is a heartnut selection from a grower in Potsdam, New York, offered by Grimo Nut Nursery for good cracking quality and a track record of ripening a crop reliably even in a short-season northern climate. It is typically grafted onto black walnut rootstock to improve vigor and productivity. Give it full sun and deep, well-drained soil, and plant a second heartnut cultivar nearby to ensure pollination.

planting.note: Plant grafted trees in early spring in deep, well-drained soil in full sun; pair with an earlier-blooming heartnut cultivar for pollination.

directions: Rose, Grimo Nut Nursery's selection Grimo 75, produces a smaller nut than most named heartnuts but is prized for cracking perfectly into decorative whole kernels nearly every time, making it popular for display and gift use as much as for eating. Its female flowers are receptive before the tree sheds its own pollen, so it needs an earlier-blooming heartnut cultivar nearby to set a full crop. Grow in full sun in deep, fertile, well-drained soil.

planting.note: Plant grafted trees in early spring in deep, well-drained soil in full sun; pair with a later-shedding heartnut cultivar for pollination.

directions: Simcoe is a heartnut selection from Grimo Nut Nursery, named for Ontario's Simcoe County, producing an unusually large, classically Valentine-heart-shaped nut that drops free as whole or half kernels with minimal effort when cracked. It is an early pollen producer, so it pairs best with later-shedding heartnut cultivars to ensure good cross-pollination. Plant in full sun in deep, well-drained soil, and expect several years of establishment before significant bearing begins.

planting.note: Plant grafted trees in early spring in deep, well-drained soil in full sun; pair with a later-blooming heartnut cultivar for pollination.

directions: Stealth, offered by Grimo Nut Nursery, bears a large, elongated nut that is a moderate but consistent producer, with kernels that drop free whole when the shell is cracked. It sheds pollen early in the season, before its own flowers are receptive, so it works best as a pollen source for later-blooming heartnut cultivars. Site it in full sun in deep, fertile, well-drained soil away from vegetable gardens.

planting.note: Plant grafted trees in early spring in deep, well-drained soil in full sun; pair with an early pollen-shedding heartnut cultivar for pollination.

directions: Wildflower, catalogued by Grimo Nut Nursery as Grimo 94, is a heartnut selection whose female flowers open before its own pollen sheds, producing whole kernels clean enough to be used as a garnish rather than just cracked for eating. Because of this early female receptivity, it should be paired with an early pollen-shedding heartnut cultivar such as Bernice, Ernie, or Stealth for reliable cross-pollination. Grow in full sun in deep, well-drained soil, siting it well away from juglone-sensitive plantings.

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container-grown grafted trees in late winter to early spring in deep, well-drained soil in full sun, well away from juglone-sensitive plants.

directions: Hays is a Nebraska-origin black walnut selection offered by Burnt Ridge Nursery, noted for a plump, well-filled kernel and a relatively thin shell for the species, which makes cracking and kernel extraction easier than with typical wild seedling trees. Plant grafted trees in deep, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun, well away from vegetable gardens and other juglone-sensitive plants. As with other named black walnut cultivars, a second genetically distinct tree nearby improves pollination and nut set, and grafted stock begins bearing years sooner than seedlings.

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container-grown grafted trees in late winter to early spring in deep, well-drained soil in full sun, well away from juglone-sensitive plants.

directions: Rowher is an Iowa-origin black walnut selection carried by Burnt Ridge Nursery, chosen for good-sized nuts with plump, well-developed kernels and overall nut quality that holds up well against other named selections. Grow grafted trees in deep, well-drained soil in full sun, siting them away from gardens and shade-sensitive species because of juglone production. A second black walnut cultivar planted nearby improves cross-pollination and yield.

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container-grown grafted trees in late winter to early spring in deep, well-drained soil in full sun, well away from juglone-sensitive plants.

directions: Surprise is a Pennsylvania-origin black walnut cultivar offered by Burnt Ridge Nursery, valued for the plump, generously filled nutmeat revealed once the shell is cracked open. Like other grafted black walnut selections, it should be planted in deep, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun, far enough from vegetable beds and sensitive ornamentals to avoid juglone injury. Pair it with another black walnut cultivar for reliable cross-pollination and plan on several years of establishment before significant bearing begins.

planting.note: Plant grafted trees in late winter to early spring; needs a second, genetically distinct chestnut nearby for cross-pollination.

directions: Ace is a Chinese hybrid chestnut selection offered as grafted or seedling stock by Empire Chestnut Company, a long-running Ohio nut nursery, alongside better-known hybrids like Szego. Like other Chinese-type chestnuts, it should be planted with a second, genetically distinct chestnut tree nearby for reliable cross-pollination and full nut set. Grow in deep, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun, and expect the first meaningful crops within a few years of grafted trees reaching bearing size.

planting.note: Plant grafted trees in late winter to early spring; needs a second, genetically distinct chestnut nearby for cross-pollination.

directions: Luvall's Monster is a Chinese hybrid chestnut cultivar listed by Empire Chestnut Company alongside its related hybrid selections Ace and Szego, intended to combine the heavier yield typical of hybrid chestnuts with the nut quality of Chinese-type parents. As with other chestnut hybrids, performance is more variable than with pure Chinese selections, so growers should expect some range in nut size and tree habit between individual trees. Plant in full sun in deep, well-drained, slightly acidic soil with a compatible pollinizer chestnut nearby.

common_name: Hong Kong Chestnut (Chinese Chestnut Seed Selection)

planting.note: Plant grafted or seedling trees in late winter to early spring; needs a second chestnut cultivar nearby for cross-pollination.

directions: Hong Kong is a Chinese chestnut selection maintained as an open-pollinated seed source by Empire Chestnut Company, offered alongside other named Chinese chestnut parent trees such as Qing, Gideon, and Peach for growers seeking seedlings selected for blight resistance, nut quality, and dependable bearing. Plant seedlings or grafted trees in deep, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun, with a second chestnut cultivar nearby to ensure good pollination. Like other Chinese chestnuts, it tolerates heat and humidity better than American or European types.

planting.note: Plant grafted or seedling trees in late winter to early spring; needs a second chestnut cultivar nearby for cross-pollination.

directions: Kohr is a named Chinese chestnut parent tree offered by Empire Chestnut Company as a source of open-pollinated seedlings selected for the blight resistance and nut-production qualities typical of improved Chinese chestnut stock. It is cataloged alongside other established Chinese chestnut selections such as AU-Homestead and Sleeping Giant. Grow in deep, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun with a second genetically distinct chestnut tree nearby for pollination.

planting.note: Plant grafted or seedling trees in late winter to early spring; needs a second chestnut cultivar nearby for cross-pollination.

directions: Liu is a Chinese chestnut selection used by Empire Chestnut Company as a named seed parent, offered to growers wanting seedlings with the blight resistance and nut characteristics selected into the nursery's Chinese chestnut breeding population. As with other Chinese chestnut selections, trees need cross-pollination from a second, unrelated chestnut tree to set a full nut crop. Plant in deep, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun, in a site with good air circulation.

planting.note: Plant grafted container stock in spring in full sun and well-drained soil, with good air circulation to reduce needlecast risk.

directions: Fat Albert is one of the most widely planted Colorado blue spruce cultivars, selected for a symmetrically dense, broadly pyramidal form and consistently good, slightly softer blue needle color compared with many other named spruce selections. It reaches a more moderate, garden-scaled height than seedling-grown Colorado spruce, making it a popular specimen or windbreak tree for properties too small for a full-size blue spruce. Plant in full sun in well-drained soil with excellent air circulation, since spruce in general is prone to needlecast diseases in humid, poorly ventilated sites. Established trees are quite drought tolerant and need little supplemental water beyond the first couple of seasons.

planting.note: Plant grafted container stock in spring in full sun and well-drained soil; give it ample room to mature into a medium to large tree.

directions: Koster is one of the oldest named Colorado blue spruce cultivars still in commerce, introduced in 1915 and long valued for its strong, consistent silvery-blue needle color on a broadly conical tree. Unlike many later blue spruce selections bred for compact size, Koster grows into a substantial medium to large specimen tree over time, so it needs a site with plenty of room to mature. Plant in full sun in well-drained soil with good air movement to reduce the needlecast disease pressure that affects spruce in humid climates, and expect slow, steady growth rather than a quick impact.

planting.note: Plant grafted container stock in spring in full sun and well-drained soil; growth is slow at first, then picks up vigor.

directions: Walnut Glen is a Colorado blue spruce selection grown primarily for its distinctive spring display, when the new shoots emerge a soft cream color before gradually greening and then taking on the species' characteristic blue cast through summer. Growth is slow for the first several years, after which the tree picks up vigor and eventually reaches full-size spruce dimensions, so plan for its eventual size even though early growth is modest. Grow in full sun in well-drained soil with good air circulation, and avoid wet, poorly drained sites that encourage needlecast and root disease.

planting.note: Plant grafted container stock in spring in full sun to very light shade and well-drained soil with good air circulation.

directions: Edith is a slow-growing dwarf Colorado blue spruce selection that can take two to five decades to reach its mature conical form, making it a long-term investment piece for rock gardens and dwarf conifer collections rather than a quick landscape specimen. Its needle color follows the typical blue-spruce pattern, intensifying in full sun. Grow in full sun to very light shade in well-drained soil, siting it where good air circulation will help prevent the needlecast diseases that trouble spruce in humid regions.

planting.note: Plant grafted container stock in spring in cool, moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to light shade.

directions: Cis is a compact dwarf selection of Korean fir that has earned the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit, staying under a few feet tall for many years while forming a dense, slow-growing mound. Like the species, it carries the glossy dark green needles with silvery undersides typical of Korean fir, and mature specimens can produce the species' attractive violet-purple cones even while still small. Grow in full sun to light shade in cool, moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil, and avoid hot, dry, or waterlogged sites, both of which stress Korean fir.

planting.note: Plant container-grown plants in spring in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil with some shelter from harsh wind and strong afternoon sun.

directions: Lycopodioides is one of the oldest named Hinoki cypress cultivars in cultivation, grown for its unusual, congested, rope-like branchlets that resemble clubmoss (Lycopodium) foliage rather than the flattened, fan-like sprays typical of the species. Growth is slow and the habit is irregular and picturesque rather than formally symmetrical, making it a conversation-piece specimen for conifer collections. Grow in full sun to light shade in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil, with some shelter from harsh winter wind and strong afternoon sun in hot climates.

planting.note: Plant in a well-drained, slightly acidic container mix or rock-garden soil in full sun to light shade; protect from prolonged drought.

directions: Minima is among the smallest named Hinoki cypress cultivars, staying under about four inches tall even after twenty years of growth, which makes it a favorite for troughs, miniature conifer gardens, and bonsai-style container culture rather than general landscape use. Its tiny scale-like foliage forms a dense, rounded tuft that increases in girth far more than in height over time. Grow in a well-drained, slightly acidic container mix or rock-garden soil in full sun to light shade, and protect from prolonged drought, since very dwarf conifers have little reserve capacity in their small root systems.

planting.note: Plant container-grown plants in spring in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil with protection from drying winter winds.

directions: Tempelhof is a medium-sized Hinoki cypress selection grown for its handsome, dense sprays of foliage that take on a bronze cast through the winter months before greening up again with the return of warm weather. It develops into an upright, broadly conical small tree over a number of years without the dramatic dwarfing of many other Hinoki cultivars. Grow in full sun to light shade in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil, with protection from drying winter winds that can scorch foliage.

planting.note: Plant container-grown plants in spring in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun for best gold color.

directions: Tsatsumi Gold is a slow-growing Hinoki cypress selection distinguished by irregularly twisted, contorted branches clothed in bright yellow-green foliage, giving it a more sculptural, informal look than the tidy fan-sprayed forms typical of the species. The gold color is strongest on growth exposed to good light, fading toward green in deeper shade. Grow in full sun to light shade in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil, siting it where its twisting branch structure can be appreciated as a textural accent.

planting.note: Plant container-grown plants in spring in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil, giving it lateral room to spread.

directions: Kamarachiba is a low, spreading Hinoki cypress selection carrying sprays of yellow-green foliage on a broad, shrubby frame rather than the upright, treelike habit of the species. Its horizontal growth makes it useful as a wide groundcover-type conifer or foreground planting in a conifer bed. Grow in full sun to light shade in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil, giving it enough lateral room to spread without crowding neighboring plants.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; shear regularly if used as a formal hedge.

directions: Atrovirens is a Royal Horticultural Society Award of Garden Merit selection of western redcedar grown for its dense, deep green foliage and reliably upright, pyramidal growth, qualities that have made it one of the standard cultivars used for tall evergreen hedging and screening in cool, moist climates. It holds its rich green color through winter better than seedling-grown western redcedar, which can bronze in cold weather. Grow in full sun to partial shade in moist, well-drained soil, and plan on a tall, substantial tree at maturity if left unclipped, or regular shearing if maintained as a formal hedge.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in moist, well-drained soil in full sun for the best gold foliage color.

directions: Aurea is an old golden-foliaged selection of western redcedar, carrying yellow to yellow-green coloring on its flattened, scale-like sprays that brightens through the growing season and provides a strong color contrast against plain green conifers. It has received the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit as a garden-worthy cultivar. Grow in full sun for the best gold color, since shaded foliage tends to revert toward green, in moist, well-drained soil typical of the species' needs.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in moist, well-drained soil in full sun for the best gold color.

directions: Stoneham Gold is a slow-growing, dwarf-to-small western redcedar selection with rich golden-yellow foliage that holds its color well through the season, making it a popular accent conifer for smaller gardens where full-size western redcedar would be unmanageable. It has received the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit. Grow in full sun for best gold color in moist, well-drained soil, and expect a dense, broadly conical habit that needs little pruning to stay tidy.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade for the brightest variegation.

directions: Zebrina is a widely planted western redcedar selection with foliage irregularly striped and banded in creamy yellow over green, giving the whole tree a soft, variegated glow that is especially bright in young growth and in full sun. It has earned the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit and is one of the more commonly available golden-variegated conifers in the nursery trade. Grow in full sun to partial shade in moist, well-drained soil, siting it where its bright coloring can serve as a focal point against plain green plantings.
